page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-240GB-1xH100 is an accelerator-focused instance configured with an NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU featuring 80 GB of VRAM. It operates on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor, delivering 12 shared vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores clocked at 2.0 GHz. The processor includes modern vector and matrix instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX, paired with 240.0 GB of system RAM, allocating 20.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with the server, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk needs. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address under KVM virtualization.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier acceleration in AI workloads. LLM inference evaluation using a small 135M parameter model reaches 10,515.12 tokens per second for prompt processing and 547.27 tokens per second for text generation, placing both metrics in the top 10% tier. CPU single-core performance registers in the top 25% with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,111.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 35.51 GB/sec. Geekbench text processing achieves a top 10% score of 2,860.0. Multi-core operations land predominantly in the average category, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 13,269.0, a PassMark CPU score of 32,078.76, and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 26,217.73.

From a qualitative cost and architectural perspective, this server prioritizes high GPU acceleration density and large memory capacity per CPU core over dense CPU core counts. The 20 GB of RAM per vCPU ratio prevents memory bottlenecks during data staging for large GPU workloads. However, the shared CPU allocation and absence of bundled local storage are tradeoffs to evaluate when running persistent or intensive parallel host-level tasks. The instance fits high-throughput deep learning inference, model fine-tuning, complex data processing pipelines, and GPU-accelerated scientific computing workloads.
